Deploy on EEZ-X mainnet

Use EEZ-X as a mainnet playground to test your contracts and integrations with the existing Ethereum ecosystem. Start with a small experiment: check the network, preview the deployment, then choose whether to broadcast. This uses real ETH; local walkthroughs remain available for simulation.

EEZ-X is live on Ethereum mainnet, with its dashboard at mainnet.eez.dev ↗. This playground is for small integration experiments, not large deposits. Transactions spend real ETH; their cost depends on the operation and current fees. The deploy command in step 4 has not yet been run end to end against this network. The dashboard reports eez-core-protocol @ 855fe06, while the walkthroughs cite 9a1f815, 11 commits later. To try the protocol at 9a1f815 in a simulation first, run the local Quickstart in an authorized environment.
1

Install Foundry

The demos and this page are pinned to Foundry v1.7.1; download the archive for your OS and architecture from the official v1.7.1 release. Verify its published checksums or attestations before extracting the tools into a directory on your PATH. Step 2 also needs a browser wallet.

SHELL
$ forge --version
$ cast --version
# Both should report version 1.7.1 after installation.
2

Fund a fresh key

Before funding, verify the official dashboard and the network settings in step 3. Use a fresh wallet and only ETH you can afford to lose, including funds bridged to the rollup. The Bridge & Calls tab of the mainnet dashboard moves real ETH to EEZ-X; this guide does not establish the bridge's security or withdrawal guarantees. Import your fresh key into an encrypted local keystore in your own terminal. Enter the private key and a strong keystore password only at the hidden prompts, outside any agent session; never put either secret in a command, environment variable or chat:

SHELL
$ cast wallet import eez-mainnet --interactive
$ export ADDR=$(cast wallet address --account eez-mainnet)

⚠ This is mainnet: transactions cost real ETH. Use a fresh key that holds only what you plan to spend here.

3

Point your shell at the network

Send transactions to the chain’s front URL. It forwards ordinary transactions, like this deploy, unchanged and composes cross-chain ones; a cross-chain call sent to the direct RPC would bypass the composer. The front also answers the reads used below; the direct RPC is for reads and protocol tooling. The L2 manager is a genesis predeploy, read from the deployment’s genesis profile (eez-rollupX @ 2c19e36 puts it at 0x4B27…402C); the L1 manager is the EEZ contract on Ethereum mainnet. Every URL, manager address and explorer in the table comes from the dashboard’s own config; the chain ids are what eth_chainId returns on each RPC.

CHAINRPC URLSCHAIN IDEEZ MANAGEREXPLORER
EEZ-X Mainnet (L2)
fronthttps://mainnet.eez.dev/composer/l2
readshttps://mainnet.eez.dev/rpc/l2
 696990 0x4B2760F84B83d6b3829E30A7573B0172B6d6402C mainnet.eez.dev/explorer
Ethereum (L1)
fronthttps://mainnet.eez.dev/composer/l1
readshttps://mainnet.eez.dev/rpc/l1
 1 0x4b2760f84b83d6b3829e30a7573b0172b6d6402c etherscan.io
SHELL · THE L2 FRONT FROM THE TABLE
$ export EEZ_RPC=https://mainnet.eez.dev/composer/l2
4

Preview, then choose whether to deploy

Replace src/MyContract.sol:MyContract with your reviewed contract and supply any required constructor arguments. Build and test it in an authorized environment first. This command checks for L2 chain ID 696990, then previews the deployment without broadcasting. It still builds your project, queries the RPC and may prompt for the local keystore password. A preview is not proof of contract or network safety.

PREVIEW · NO BROADCAST
$ test "$(cast chain-id --rpc-url "$EEZ_RPC")" = "696990" &&
  forge create src/MyContract.sol:MyContract --rpc-url "$EEZ_RPC" --chain-id 696990 --account eez-mainnet

If the chain check fails, stop and investigate the endpoint; do not bypass it. A matching chain ID alone does not authenticate an RPC. Review the account, contract, constructor arguments, value and estimated fees before continuing.

Send the deployment on EEZ-X mainnet — spends real ETH

Only run this after deciding to spend real ETH on this deployment. If an agent is helping, authorize this specific broadcast separately. Use the same reviewed contract and arguments as the preview.

MAINNET BROADCAST · REAL ETH
$ test "$(cast chain-id --rpc-url "$EEZ_RPC")" = "696990" &&
  forge create src/MyContract.sol:MyContract --rpc-url "$EEZ_RPC" --chain-id 696990 --account eez-mainnet --broadcast
EXPECTED OUTPUT · NOT A COMMAND
Deployer: 0x…
Deployed to: 0x…   ← verify the receipt and deployed code
Transaction hash: 0x…

After a broadcast, check the transaction receipt and the deployed address on the intended chain. Replace the quoted placeholder below with that address. Non-empty bytecode only establishes that code exists; compare it and the constructor configuration with your expected deployment. It does not prove cross-chain settlement or contract safety.

SHELL
$ cast code "DEPLOYED_CONTRACT_ADDRESS" --rpc-url "$EEZ_RPC"
5

If it fails

insufficient funds

The key isn't funded on the EEZ-X rollup — move ETH over with the dashboard's Bridge & Calls tab on mainnet.eez.dev, then cast balance $ADDR --rpc-url $EEZ_RPC to confirm before retrying.

connection refused / timeout

$EEZ_RPC doesn't match the table in step 3 — re-copy it. cast chain-id --rpc-url $EEZ_RPC should print the chain id from the table.

nonce too low / no receipt yet

Inspect the original transaction hash and the account's nonce before taking action. A missing receipt is not proof that the transaction was rejected. Do not automatically resend, replace or send additional funds; first establish whether the original transaction is pending, mined or failed.
